objects.description: Class representing a JSON value of varying type (null, string, bool, number, array, object). It owns the underlying data via a discriminated union with heap-allocated members for string/array/object and provides parsing and stringification helpers as well as accessors and child navigation.
Utility class providing static functions to parse JSON text into JSONValue trees and to stringify JSONValue trees back to text. Not intended to be instantiated (private constructor).
Alias for a dynamic array (std::vector) of pointers to JSONValue, representing a JSON array. The vector owns pointers by convention but lifetime management is manual and not specified here.
Alias for an associative container mapping strings to JSONValue pointers, representing a JSON object. Pointer lifetime management is manual and handled by JSONValue implementation.

objects.definition: enum JSONType { JSONType_Null, JSONType_String, JSONType_Bool, JSONType_Number, JSONType_Array, JSONType_Object };
objects.description: Enumeration of the possible types that a JSONValue can hold.

functions.name: simplejson_csnlen
functions.signature: static inline bool simplejson_csnlen(const char *s, size_t n)
functions.description: Checks whether the C-string pointer s has at least n non-null characters before the terminating '\0'. Returns false if s is null or if a null terminator is encountered before n characters.
requirements: s may be null; if null the function returns false.
s is expected to point to a null-terminated C-string buffer; the function will read up to n bytes or until a '\0' is found.

n is the minimum number of characters to verify; no specific range is enforced, but extremely large n may cause out-of-bounds reads if s does not have that many accessible bytes (caller must ensure readable memory).

functions.name: JSON::Parse
functions.description: Parses a null-terminated JSON text from data and returns a dynamically created JSONValue tree representing the parsed content. Intended as the main entry point to parse JSON into the library's DOM structure.
requirements: data should be a non-null pointer to a null-terminated buffer containing JSON text.
The input should be valid JSON; behavior on invalid JSON is unspecified (may return nullptr or a null/invalid value).
Caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of the returned JSONValue pointer (ownership semantics are not documented here and are unknown).

functions.name: JSON::Stringify
functions.description: Serializes the provided JSONValue tree to a JSON-formatted string. Produces a compact JSON representation.
requirements: value should be a non-null pointer to a valid JSONValue instance; behavior for nullptr is unspecified.
The provided JSONValue and any nested nodes must be in a valid state (types consistent).

functions.name: JSONValue::JSONValue
functions.description: Constructs a JSONValue representing JSON null.
requirements: No arguments; resulting value represents null.

functions.name: JSONValue::JSONValue
functions.description: Constructs a JSONValue of type string from a C-string.
requirements: m_char_value should be a non-null pointer to a null-terminated C-string.
Encoding/validation of contents is unspecified.

functions.name: JSONValue::JSONValue
functions.description: Constructs a JSONValue of type string from a std::string.
requirements: m_string_value is a valid std::string reference.

functions.name: JSONValue::JSONValue
functions.description: Constructs a JSONValue of type boolean.
requirements: No special requirements beyond providing a boolean value.

functions.name: JSONValue::JSONValue
functions.description: Constructs a JSONValue of type number from a double.
requirements: m_number_value should be a finite numeric value; special values (NaN/Inf) handling is unspecified.

functions.name: JSONValue::JSONValue
functions.description: Constructs a JSONValue of type number from a signed integer.
requirements: No special requirements beyond providing an integer value.

functions.name: JSONValue::JSONValue
functions.description: Constructs a JSONValue of type number from an unsigned integer.
requirements: No special requirements beyond providing an unsigned integer value.

functions.name: JSONValue::JSONValue
functions.description: Constructs a JSONValue of type array from a JSONArray (std::vector<JSONValue*>).
requirements: m_array_value should contain pointers to valid JSONValue instances; null element pointers may lead to undefined behavior (not specified).
Ownership/lifetime of element pointers is not documented here and is unknown.

functions.name: JSONValue::JSONValue
functions.description: Constructs a JSONValue of type object from a JSONObject (std::map<std::string, JSONValue*>).
requirements: m_object_value should contain keys as std::string and values as pointers to valid JSONValue instances; null value pointers may lead to undefined behavior (not specified).
Ownership/lifetime of value pointers is not documented here and is unknown.

functions.name: JSONValue::~JSONValue
functions.description: Destructor for JSONValue. Cleans up any resources held by the value (including any dynamically allocated substructures for strings, arrays, or objects).
requirements: After destruction, the JSONValue must not be used.
If external code holds raw pointers to elements contained within this value (e.g., array/object members), those pointers become invalid after destruction.

functions.name: JSONValue::IsNull
functions.description: Returns true if this value is of type null.
requirements: The JSONValue object must be valid.

functions.name: JSONValue::IsString
functions.description: Returns true if this value is of type string.
requirements: The JSONValue object must be valid.

functions.name: JSONValue::IsBool
functions.description: Returns true if this value is of type boolean.
requirements: The JSONValue object must be valid.

functions.name: JSONValue::IsNumber
functions.description: Returns true if this value is of type number.
requirements: The JSONValue object must be valid.

functions.name: JSONValue::IsArray
functions.description: Returns true if this value is of type array.
requirements: The JSONValue object must be valid.

functions.name: JSONValue::IsObject
functions.description: Returns true if this value is of type object.
requirements: The JSONValue object must be valid.

functions.name: JSONValue::AsString
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the underlying string value.
requirements: Call only when IsString() is true; otherwise behavior is unspecified/invalid.

functions.name: JSONValue::AsBool
functions.description: Returns the underlying boolean value.
requirements: Call only when IsBool() is true; otherwise behavior is unspecified/invalid.

functions.name: JSONValue::AsNumber
functions.description: Returns the underlying numeric value as a double.
requirements: Call only when IsNumber() is true; otherwise behavior is unspecified/invalid.

functions.name: JSONValue::AsArray
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the underlying array (vector of JSONValue*).
requirements: Call only when IsArray() is true; otherwise behavior is unspecified/invalid.
Elements are raw pointers; ownership/lifetime is not documented and is unknown.

functions.name: JSONValue::AsObject
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the underlying object (map<string, JSONValue*>).
requirements: Call only when IsObject() is true; otherwise behavior is unspecified/invalid.
Values are raw pointers; ownership/lifetime is not documented and is unknown.

functions.name: JSONValue::CountChildren
functions.description: Returns the number of children if the value is an array or object; otherwise likely returns 0 (exact behavior not specified).
requirements: The JSONValue object must be valid.
For arrays, counts elements; for objects, counts key-value pairs (inferred).

functions.name: JSONValue::HasChild
functions.description: Checks whether an array value has a child at the given zero-based index.
requirements: Call only when IsArray() is true; otherwise behavior is unspecified/invalid.
index should be less than CountChildren() to be considered present.

functions.name: JSONValue::HasChild
functions.description: Checks whether an object value contains a field with the given name.
requirements: Call only when IsObject() is true; otherwise behavior is unspecified/invalid.
name should be a non-null pointer to a null-terminated C-string.

functions.name: JSONValue::Child
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the array element at the given zero-based index.
requirements: Call only when IsArray() is true; otherwise behavior is unspecified/invalid.
index must be within range [0, CountChildren()).

functions.name: JSONValue::Child
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the object field's value with the given name, if present.
requirements: Call only when IsObject() is true; otherwise behavior is unspecified/invalid.
name should be a non-null pointer to a null-terminated C-string.
If the key is not present, the function may return nullptr (exact behavior not specified).

functions.name: JSONValue::ObjectKeys
functions.description: Returns a vector containing all keys of the object value.
requirements: Call only when IsObject() is true; otherwise behavior is unspecified/invalid.

functions.name: JSONValue::Stringify
functions.signature: std::string JSONValue::Stringify(bool const prettyprint = false) const
functions.description: Serializes this JSONValue to a JSON-formatted string. If prettyprint is true, output may be formatted with indentation and newlines.
requirements: The JSONValue must be in a valid state.
prettyprint controls formatting only; content fidelity depends on the stored types and values.

data_types.description: A null-terminated sequence of bytes accessible via const char*. May contain arbitrary bytes except it must include a terminating '\0'. Not required to be valid UTF-8.

Textual JSON data encoded as a null-terminated string. May represent any valid JSON value (object, array, string, number, boolean, or null). Whitespace and formatting per RFC 7159/ECMA-404 are allowed.

generators.generator:
import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator creates valid, interesting C-string buffers intended for fuzzing
# simple JSON parsing and JSONValue object/array navigation stubs that use
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR and C-string pointers. We focus on producing null-terminated
# buffers that are valid JSON or valid object/array keys to exercise:
# - JSON::Parse (general JSON documents)
# - JSONValue::HasChild / Child (arrays and objects with various key/index cases)
# - simplejson_csnlen (strings with/without early NUL, varying lengths)
#
# Strategy:
# 1) Produce a mix of JSON values: null, booleans, numbers, strings (with escapes),
#    arrays, and objects, including nested structures and edge cases like empty
#    containers, duplicate keys, and mixed-type arrays.
# 2) Ensure the output is a null-terminated bytes buffer.
# 3) Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
# 4) Include some buffers that consist solely of C-string content useful for
#    name-based lookups (e.g., common and unusual keys), as the stubs sometimes
#    pass random strings for object key probes.
#
# All outputs are intended to be valid JSON or valid C-strings, not malformed.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

# Common keys and values to help object lookups succeed
COMMON_KEYS = [
    "id", "name", "value", "type", "data", "items", "children", "child",
    "config", "settings", "enabled", "disabled", "true", "false",
    "null", "count", "index", "0", "1", "key", "keys",
    "a", "b", "c", "long_key_name", "nested", "array", "object",
]

ESCAPABLE_CHARS = ["\\\"/bfnrt"]  # just to hint inclusion of escape sequences


def _rand(rng: random.Random, seq: List[str]):
    return seq[rng.randrange(len(seq))]


def gen_whitespace(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # JSON allows insignificant whitespace around values and separators
    choices = ["", " ", "\t", "\n", "\r", " \n", "\t \r"]
    return _rand(rng, choices)


def gen_number(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate JSON number forms
    forms = []
    ints = [
        "0", "1", "-1", "10", "-10", "123456789", str(rng.randint(-2**31, 2**31 - 1)),
    ]
    forms.extend(ints)
    # decimal
    sign = "-" if rng.random() < 0.5 else ""
    intpart = str(rng.randint(0, 999999))
    frac = str(rng.randint(0, 999999)).rjust(rng.randint(1, 6), "0")
    forms.append(f"{sign}{intpart}.{frac}")
    # exponent
    base = str(rng.randint(1, 9999))
    exp = str(rng.randint(-20, 20))
    forms.append(f"{base}e{exp}")
    forms.append(f"{base}E+{abs(int(exp))}")
    return _rand(rng, forms)


def gen_string(rng: random.Random, min_len=0, max_len=64, allow_escapes=True) -> str:
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Include a mix of ASCII, spaces, punctuation; avoid raw NUL in JSON strings
    alphabet = (string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-:/.,{}[]()@#%&+*=|~^$")
    s = [rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length)]
    s = "".join(s)
    if allow_escapes and length > 0 and rng.random() < 0.7:
        # inject some JSON escapes
        escapes = ['\\"', "\\\\", "\\n", "\\r", "\\t", "\\b", "\\f"]
        pos = rng.randrange(len(s))
        s = s[:pos] + _rand(rng, escapes) + s[pos:]
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        # bias toward common key names as entire string
        s = _rand(rng, COMMON_KEYS)
    return '"' + s + '"'


def gen_bool_or_null(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return _rand(rng, ["true", "false", "null"])


def gen_array(rng: random.Random, depth: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(0, 8)
    elems = []
    for _ in range(n):
        elems.append(gen_value(rng, depth + 1))
    # insert whitespace variation
    sep = "," + gen_whitespace(rng)
    inside_ws_l = gen_whitespace(rng)
    inside_ws_r = gen_whitespace(rng)
    return f"[{inside_ws_l}{sep.join(elems)}{inside_ws_r}]"


def gen_object(rng: random.Random, depth: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(0, 8)
    # ensure at least one common key occasionally to help lookups succeed
    keys = set()
    items = []
    if n > 0 and rng.random() < 0.7:
        k = _rand(rng, COMMON_KEYS)
        keys.add(k)
        items.append('"' + k + '"' + ":" + gen_whitespace(rng) + gen_value(rng, depth + 1))
    while len(items) < n:
        # random key; avoid duplicates
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            k = _rand(rng, COMMON_KEYS)
        else:
            k = gen_string(rng, 0, 16, allow_escapes=False)[1:-1]
        if k in keys:
            continue
        keys.add(k)
        items.append('"' + k + '"' + ":" + gen_whitespace(rng) + gen_value(rng, depth + 1))
    # possible duplicate key to exercise map behavior in parser/DOM (still valid JSON)
    if n > 1 and rng.random() < 0.3:
        dup = _rand(rng, list(keys))
        items.append('"' + dup + '"' + ":" + gen_whitespace(rng) + gen_value(rng, depth + 1))
    sep = "," + gen_whitespace(rng)
    inside_ws_l = gen_whitespace(rng)
    inside_ws_r = gen_whitespace(rng)
    return f"{{{inside_ws_l}{sep.join(items)}{inside_ws_r}}}"


def gen_value(rng: random.Random, depth: int = 0) -> str:
    # depth control to avoid excessive nesting
    if depth > 4:
        pick = rng.random()
        if pick < 0.3:
            return gen_string(rng)
        elif pick < 0.6:
            return gen_number(rng)
        else:
            return gen_bool_or_null(rng)
    choices = [
        lambda: gen_string(rng),
        lambda: gen_number(rng),
        lambda: gen_bool_or_null(rng),
        lambda: gen_array(rng, depth),
        lambda: gen_object(rng, depth),
    ]
    # weight toward objects/arrays to support Child/HasChild
    weights = [0.2, 0.2, 0.1, 0.25, 0.25]
    r = rng.random()
    acc = 0.0
    for f, w in zip(choices, weights):
        acc += w
        if r <= acc:
            return f()
    return choices[-1]()


def gen_document(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Surround with optional whitespace to mimic real-world inputs
    ws_l = gen_whitespace(rng)
    ws_r = gen_whitespace(rng)
    return ws_l + gen_value(rng, 0) + ws_r


def gen_key_only_string(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Used to probe HasChild/Child(name) with a single key value as C-string buffer
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        s = _rand(rng, COMMON_KEYS)
    else:
        s = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_- ") for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 32)))
    return s


def maybe_embed_early_nul(rng: random.Random, data: bytes) -> bytes:
    # For simplejson_csnlen: sometimes place an early NUL before true end
    if len(data) == 0 or rng.random() < 0.5:
        return data + b"\x00"
    pos = rng.randint(0, min(len(data), 64))  # early in buffer to keep n small
    return data[:pos] + b"\x00" + data[pos:]


def assemble_buffer(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Choose among several buffer themes
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.55:
        # Full JSON document
        doc = gen_document(rng)
        b = doc.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')
        # Ensure proper terminal NUL, possibly with early NUL for csnlen
        b = maybe_embed_early_nul(rng, b)
    elif choice < 0.75:
        # Pure key string C-buffer (not JSON), useful for name probes
        key = gen_key_only_string(rng)
        b = key.encode('utf-8', errors='strict') + b"\x00"
    else:
        # Compact arrays/objects with many children to stress CountChildren/indices
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            # wide array
            arr = '[' + ','.join(gen_number(rng) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 32))) + ']'
            b = maybe_embed_early_nul(rng, arr.encode('utf-8'))
        else:
            # object with many predictable keys
            kvs = []
            for i in range(rng.randint(1, 24)):
                k = _rand(rng, COMMON_KEYS) if rng.random() < 0.7 else f"k{i}"
                v = gen_value(rng, 1)
                kvs.append('"' + k + '"' + ':' + v)
            obj = '{' + ','.join(kvs) + '}'
            b = maybe_embed_early_nul(rng, obj.encode('utf-8'))

    # Enforce size limit by truncating before final NUL then re-terminating
    if len(b) > MAX_SIZE:
        # ensure there is at least one byte room for NUL terminator
        b = b[: MAX_SIZE - 1]
        # remove any embedded NUL at end and re-terminate cleanly
        if b and b[-1] == 0:
            b = b[:-1]
        b = b + b"\x00"
    else:
        # Ensure at least one terminator at end
        if not b or b[-1] != 0:
            b = b + b"\x00"
    return b


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    return assemble_buffer(rng)
